top_story: Israeli far-right ministers escalated pressure on one of the region’s most combustible flashpoints on 23 July by leading a mass incursion into the Al-Aqsa compound, where thousands entered under official protection, raised Israeli flags, and openly challenged the site’s long-standing status quo. That provocation unfolded against the continuing baseline of lethal Israeli air operations in Gaza that are repeatedly killing children, reinforcing across Palestinian society a sense that civilian life and sacred space are both under sustained assault. By 24 July, violence in the occupied West Bank had sharpened further when a settler attack involving gunfire and, by residents’ account, Israeli military participation left four Palestinians and one Israeli dead. The sequence points to a deepening cycle in which state-backed nationalist escalation in Jerusalem and persistent mass harm in Gaza are feeding wider territorial violence and accelerating Palestinian insecurity far beyond a single front.
